brief: UBS CIO reviews NVIDIA's 3QFY27 results, released after cofounder and CEO Jensen Huang's departure. Revenue of USD 115.8bn and non-GAAP EPS of USD 2.68 beat consensus of USD 109.0bn and USD 2.48. Data center revenue reached USD 107.6bn, up 110% y/y: hyperscaler revenue grew 71% y/y to USD 60.1bn off a tough 125% prior-year comp, and ACIE revenue grew 195% y/y to USD 41.5bn on Vera Rubin shipments to neoclouds and frontier labs building their own data centers. Gross margin (74.9%) and operating margin (67.2%) both beat consensus. Guidance for the January 2027 quarter, USD 130.0bn excluding China, topped consensus; gross margin is guided to 71.0-72.0%, bracketing a 4QFY27 trough from absorbing higher supply costs before new pricing, then recovering to 72-73% in FY28. Management raised FY28 revenue growth guidance to about 75% from 70% on stronger demand and supply, so UBS expects mid- to high-single-digit earnings-estimate upgrades. The board is weighing internal and external CEO candidates. NVIDIA will be more selective on customer financing going forward, leaning more on third-party financing partners. A new USD 150bn buyback brings total capacity to USD 227bn. UBS stays constructive but notes this is the fourth year of the AI rally, where incremental capex alone may not be enough and investors will focus more on monetization.
